title: Find The Duplicate Number
description:
An array nums contains n + 1 integers whose values are all between 1 and n, inclusive. Exactly one distinct value occurs more than once; it might appear two times or many times. Return that repeated value, not its index or its frequency.

Do not modify nums, and use only constant additional space. These restrictions rule out sorting in place or building a set of seen values. At least two elements are present, so a duplicate always exists. Equal adjacent positions in the input are not guaranteed.

The interesting connection is to linked-list cycles even though the input is an array: treat each value as a pointer to another index. Following those pointers eventually repeats an index, and the entry point of that cycle identifies the duplicate. A slow pointer and a fast pointer can locate it without modifying the array.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [1,3,4,2,2]
Output: 2

Example 2:

Input: nums = [3,1,3,4,2]
Output: 3

Example 3:

Input: nums = [1,1]
Output: 1

Constraints:

  • 1 <= n <= 10,000 and nums.length = n + 1.
  • 1 <= nums[i] <= n.
  • Exactly one distinct number is duplicated, possibly more than twice.
